page: Microsoft Azure D64ls_v5 is a compute-focused instance within the general-purpose Dls_v5 series, tailored for workloads that require high CPU density without large memory allocations. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine delivers 64 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 32 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, accompanied by 48 KB L1d cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Advanced vector extensions including AVX-512 and cryptographic offloads such as VAES and SHA-NI are available at the instruction level.

Memory capacity is configured at 128 GB, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per vCPU). The instance features no bundled local storage, requiring remote Premium Storage for operating system and data volumes. In benchmark testing, the D64ls_v5 exhibits strong uncached memory bandwidth, reaching 292.88 GB/sec in large-block reads and 135.25 GB/sec in writes. Multi-core compute throughput is robust, evident in a Geekbench multi-core score of 16,569 and a PassMark CPU score of 60,731.27.

Application-level benchmarks demonstrate high capability in concurrent operations, with Redis SET throughput achieving 61.81 million operations per second and static web serving reaching 53.15 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core metrics fall into the average range, and large language model inference shows diminished performance on larger parameter models due to the absence of dedicated accelerators.

Cost efficiency is optimized for parallel compute, software compilation, and scalable web services that do not require extensive RAM per core. Tradeoffs center on the absence of ephemeral local disk space and standard memory density, positioning the instance for distributed computing clusters, CI/CD compilation pipelines, batch processing, and high-concurrency web tiers.
description: Microsoft Azure D64ls_v5 provides 64 dedicated vCPUs and 128 GB of RAM powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor on Microsoft Hyper-V. Characterized by a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this configuration favors CPU-dense processing over memory capacity. The instance includes AVX-512 vector support and robust cryptographic instruction sets, but omits bundled local storage and hardware GPU acceleration. Benchmark assessments highlight strong multi-core execution, demonstrated by a PassMark CPU score of 60,731.27 and uncached memory read bandwidth of 292.88 GB/sec. High-throughput static web serving and Redis caching run efficiently, while single-thread performance remains moderate. The instance represents an economical compute tier for distributed batch operations, Clang compilation, and scalable microservices.
